title: Downtown Los Angeles on I-5: Exits, Skyline, Services
meta: Downtown Los Angeles on I-5 runs from exit 129 to exit 137B, with the skyline at exit 133, the East LA Interchange near exit 134, and listed gas and food.
intro: I-5 passes Downtown Los Angeles between about exit 129 and exit 137B, with the skyline of towers rising to the west across the Los Angeles River near exit 133. This page lists the nearby exits, landmarks such as the East Los Angeles Interchange, and the gas, EV, food and lodging mapped at each exit. Services come from OpenStreetMap as mapped, not live.

faq.q: What exit is Downtown Los Angeles on I-5?
faq.a: The Downtown Los Angeles skyline is noted at exit 133, Grande Vista Avenue. Other nearby exits include 135B for Cesar Chavez Avenue, 136B for Broadway and 136A for Main Street.

faq.q: Where do I-5, I-10, US 101 and CA 60 meet near Downtown LA?
faq.a: They meet at the East Los Angeles Interchange near exit 134, on the left going north, a tangle of ramps spread over 135 acres of Boyle Heights. Exit 134B is Soto Street and CA 60 East toward Pomona, and exit 135C is I-10 East toward San Bernardino.

faq.q: Is there gas near Downtown Los Angeles on I-5?
faq.a: Yes, gas stations are listed at many exits here, such as 3 at exit 133, 4 at exit 134A and 4 at exit 135C. This comes from OpenStreetMap as mapped, not live, so it does not show what is open or what it costs.

faq.q: Where is the nearest rest area to Downtown Los Angeles on I-5?
faq.a: Going south, the nearest is Aliso Creek Rest Area at mile 59.4, 73.6 miles from here. Going north, it is Tejon Pass Rest Area at mile 206.1, 73.1 miles from here, and both are open to both directions of travel.

faq.q: What can I see from I-5 in Downtown Los Angeles?
faq.a: Near exit 133 the towers of downtown rise to the west, including the Wilshire Grand Center with its thin spire, finished in 2017. Near exit 134 on the left going north is the old Sears, Roebuck mail-order tower, finished in 1927 in 171 days.
